summary: A narrow-column, magazine-like page for a high-contrast grotesque, built on Lost Type's earlier 'BigIdeasText' template: headline blocks are contenteditable and re-fit line by line to the column, each flagged with a small blue 'Edit Me!' sticker. Between them sit full-width colour bands (a two-colour riso glyph poster in live SVG text, a weight ramp, a live clock) and a long first-person origin story about a Rollfast bicycle logo and the designer's grandfather.

instances.look: White page, short red bar on top, 'Introducing' kicker, red Black-weight 'MORISTON' with a tilted blue 'Edit Me!' sticker on its corner, then 'A sans-serif typeface with / unusually high contrast—and enthusiasm!' in two weights, 'by Riley Cran' and a short intro paragraph
instances.ux: Name and tagline form one contenteditable block: click to retype the hero; each line re-fits to the column width
instances.learn: A tiny 'Edit Me!' sticker on the headline turns the hero itself into a tester without adding any controls

reconstruction.layout: Centred column 720px wide in a 1440 page, ~1050px tall block; red bar 720×20px at the very top; kicker, headline block (3 lines, each fitted to 720px), byline, ~17px intro paragraph, then a grey promo card (see checkout)
reconstruction.typography: 'MORISTON' ~110px Moriston 900 uppercase red; line 2 ~44px Moriston 400; line 3 ~30px 400 with 'and enthusiasm!' in 600; kicker and byline ~14px 400 grey; sticker ~11px white on blue, rotated about −5°; body ~17px 400
reconstruction.behaviour: BigIdeasText script sizes every span (.bigIdeasText-lineN) so each line fills the container width, and refits on input (min font size 20px); no animation
reconstruction.content: Real tagline: 'A sans-serif typeface with unusually high contrast—and enthusiasm!' and positioning copy (6 weights, 200+ languages, number styles)
reconstruction.assets: none in the hero itself (the promo card below uses a riso print photo)
reconstruction.html: header.story-header > span.story-intro + div.is-editable.simpleTester.js-scaleText.bigIdeasText[contenteditable][bigideastext-minfontsize=20] > h1.bigIdeasText-line0 + span.bigIdeasText-line1/2; the 'Edit Me!' tag is a CSS ::before on .is-editable

instances.look: Light-grey card: photo of the two-colour riso poster on a wooden table at left; at right 'Pay-What-You-Want for a Personal Use License. Purchase a Commercial Use License for $75 and receive a kickass risograph print at no extra charge!' and a red 'Get Moriston' button
instances.ux: The whole card is one link to the Lost Type shop page; the same card is repeated at the end of the story (block 06)
instances.learn: Bundle a physical print with the commercial licence and show its photo in the buy card: buying feels like patronage, not a transaction

reconstruction.layout: Card 720px wide (column width), ~250px tall, light grey; two equal cells: photo (~290×190px) left, text + button right; button full cell width ~320×56px
reconstruction.typography: Card text ~18px Moriston 400 grey with lining figures (lnum); button label ~16px 600 white
reconstruction.content: Pay-what-you-want personal licence, $75 commercial licence with a free riso print

instances.look: A tall 3×4 grid of square tiles, each holding one giant cropped glyph (7, @, 5, S, &, ®, m, ?, %, Q, £…), overprinted in coral red and blue so overlaps go navy and glyph-on-glyph knocks out white
instances.learn: Recreate the bonus print as live SVG text: two layers of cropped glyphs multiplied together give a riso overprint look with real font outlines

reconstruction.layout: Near-full-bleed band (1380px wide, ~1840px tall), SVG viewBox 600×800 = 3 columns × 4 rows of 200-unit squares; no gutters
reconstruction.typography: One glyph per square at 340–400 SVG units (≈780–920px rendered), Moriston weights 400–900, white, positioned so it overflows and is clipped by its square
reconstruction.behaviour: none; two <g> layers ('blue-layer', 'red-layer'), each a grid of coloured squares with white glyphs, combined with mix-blend-mode: multiply so square×square = navy, glyph over square = the other colour, glyph×glyph = white
reconstruction.content: Mixed figures, lowercase, caps and symbols (6 5 a s p 2 ß Q m G m % 7 M @ 0 d & ® ? 8 V 4 £)
reconstruction.assets: none (inline SVG with <text> in the webfont)
reconstruction.html: div.section.riso > svg[viewBox='0 0 600 800'] > g#blue-layer|#red-layer > g.svg-square > rect + clipPath + text

instances.look: 'MORISTON' three times in red Black caps, each with a long black stepped drop shadow running down-right, 'EDIT ME!' sticker on the first line
instances.ux: The stack is one editable block that keeps every line fitted to the column (max font size 1000px)
instances.learn: A hard extruded shadow in CSS makes the heaviest weight look like a painted sign while staying live, editable text

reconstruction.layout: White band ~810px tall, centred 720px column; three lines fitted to the column width, tight leading (~0.85); shadow overflows right (section--crop clips it)
reconstruction.behaviour: Stacked text-shadow (many 1px steps down-right in black) for the extrusion; BigIdeasText refits on input

instances.variantDefinition: Editable display lines that each rescale their font size to fill the column width as you type; no size or axis controls, at most one button that switches the style of the whole stack.
instances.look: On saturated blue, six white lines stepping from Light to Black, all justified to the same width: 'Airplane travels', 'ROLLFAST BICYCLE', 'Scottish River Glens', 'LOCAL LOCH', 'Very good Jazz albums', 'New York'
instances.ux: One editable block; every line is re-fitted to the column, so typed text always forms a justified weight ramp
instances.learn: Fit every line of a weight ramp to the same measure: the weights read as a clean block, and the default words retell the origin story (bicycle, Scotland, New York)

reconstruction.layout: Full-bleed blue band ~1080px tall; centred 720px column; six lines, each fitted to 720px, ~30px gaps
reconstruction.typography: Moriston weights 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 900 in order; sizes from fitting ≈54–127px (shortest line biggest); mixed case and all caps alternating; white
reconstruction.behaviour: BigIdeasText fit-to-width per line, recalculated on input
reconstruction.content: Words from the design story: airplane travels, Rollfast bicycle, Scottish river glens, local loch, jazz albums, New York

instances.look: A working analogue clock on white: numerals 1–12 in light Moriston around an empty face, thick black hour and minute hands, a thin red second hand with a small square-outlined tip
instances.ux: Live: the hands are rotated by JavaScript every second to the visitor's local time
instances.learn: A live object (a ticking clock) shows off the numerals at display size and keeps a quiet section moving

reconstruction.layout: White band ~840px tall; clock ~520px diameter centred; numerals placed on a circle (ol.clock-numbers), hands pivot at the centre; section--crop clips it on small screens
reconstruction.typography: Numerals ~52px Moriston Light (300), tabular feel, dark grey; two-digit numbers (10–12) slightly condensed spacing (.clock-double)
reconstruction.behaviour: setInterval each second: transform: rotate() on #js-clockS (6°/s), #js-clockM and #js-clockH computed from the current time

instances.variantDefinition: A heading plus the full alphabetical list of supported language names, set small as running text or in columns; the list is the proof, no sample sentences.
instances.look: On charcoal, the white heading 'Moriston speaks your language' and below it ~225 Latin-script language names (Abenaki … Zuni) as one comma-separated paragraph flowing through three columns
instances.ux: Both the heading and the list are contenteditable (same BigIdeasText fitting as elsewhere)
instances.learn: Flow the whole language list as one small paragraph in columns: it reads as texture from afar and as a checklist up close, and doubles as a text-size specimen

reconstruction.layout: Dark band ~800px tall; wider 'breakout' container (~1100px); heading centred; list in 3 CSS columns with ~40px gap
reconstruction.typography: Heading ~61px Moriston 600–700 white; list ~12px Moriston 400 light grey, leading ~1.4

instances.look: 'Fall 2015' dateline and an editable 'READ MORISTON' title, a large lede paragraph, then a narrow article column with a full-width photo of the Rollfast bicycle 'R' badge on grey, an interpolation proof (outline 'Moriston' at five weights with point coordinates), subheads 'Glenmoriston' and 'At first, light', and two riso-poster photos
instances.feel: Intimate, like a long blog post from the designer
instances.ux: Long read; title and dateline editable; captions link to the shop
instances.learn: Tell the origin as a found object (a bicycle logotype seen in Soho) plus a family dedication: the name and the letterforms both get a story

reconstruction.layout: Article column ~600px (lede ~720px) centred; figures break out to ~1100px on light-grey (#f6f6f6) bands with captions under them; interpolation figure 75% + caption 25% side column; ~6900px tall in total
reconstruction.typography: Title ~100px Moriston 900 uppercase, two lines; lede ~24px 400; body ~16px 400, leading ~1.5; subheads ~24px 700; captions ~14px grey; 'Fall 2015' kicker ~14px with lnum
reconstruction.content: First-person story: Rollfast bicycle logotype in Soho, Benton Gothic and Miller & Richards Grotesque #7 references, grandfather Glenn Morison Chronister and Glenmoriston, interpolation process
